title: Constructor Functions and Inheritance
concept: A constructor function's prototype property becomes the [[Prototype]] of objects created with new

steps.title: Adding a method to Animal.prototype
steps.explanation:
Adding the `eat` method to `Animal.prototype`.
All instances of `Animal` will share this `eat` method through the prototype chain.
steps.keyInsight: Adding a method to prototype = all instances share it

steps.title: Dog constructor + calling the parent constructor
steps.explanation:
Inside the `Dog` constructor, we call `Animal.call(this, name)`.
This passes the new object (`this`) to the `Animal` constructor, initializing the `name` property — the same role as `super()` in a class.
steps.keyInsight: Animal.call(this) = running the parent constructor (acts like super())

steps.title: Connecting the prototype chain
steps.explanation:
`Object.create(Animal.prototype)` creates a new empty object whose prototype is `Animal.prototype`, and assigns it to `Dog.prototype`.
This establishes the inheritance relationship between `Dog` and `Animal`.

steps.title: Adding a method to Dog.prototype
steps.explanation:
Adding the `bark` method to `Dog.prototype`.
Now instances of `Dog` can use both `bark` and `eat`.

steps.title: Creating an instance
steps.explanation:
Creating the `buddy` instance with `new Dog('Buddy')`.
During creation, `Animal.call` runs so `buddy.name` is set to 'Buddy', and `buddy`'s `[[Prototype]]` points to `Dog.prototype`.

steps.title: Accessing its own property
steps.explanation:
Looking up `buddy.name`.
The `name` property exists directly on `buddy`, so 'Buddy' is returned immediately.

steps.title: Calling a parent prototype method
steps.explanation:
Looking up `buddy.eat()`.
It's not on `buddy` itself, so the chain is traversed and `eat` is found on `Animal.prototype`.

steps.title: Calling a child prototype method
steps.explanation:
Looking up `buddy.bark()`.
It's not on `buddy`, but `bark` is found on `Dog.prototype` (the next step in the chain).

quiz.question: What happens if you leave out Dog.prototype.constructor = Dog;?
quiz.explanation:
When you create a new object with Object.create(), it has no constructor property.
The chain is then traversed to find Animal.prototype.constructor (= Animal).

misconceptions.correct:
This makes Dog.prototype and Animal.prototype the same object.
Any method added to Dog also gets added to Animal.
misconceptions.why: You must use Object.create() to create a new intermediate object and link it.
